newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks shrug rates woes on Wall St. rally.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks shrug rates woes on Wall St. rally.

text.p: Mexican shares shook off their early lethargy to notch up sharp gains in late morning trade on Monday and cross the 3,900-point mark for the first time since February.
Dealers said sharp gains on Wall Street dispelled fears of forthcoming possible U.S. interest rate hikes.
"They were indecisive this morning, but there are no doubts about the Dow now," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 27.85 points, or 0.72 percent, at 3,901.23.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was meanwhile up 102.20 points and just shy of an earlier intraday record high at 7,271.73.

"I feel many investors were on the sidelines because of the FOMC meeting. Foreign investors seem to be waiting for the right moment to come back, they're there, but still selective," the trader added.
The Federal Open Market Committee will meet May 20 to review U.S. interest rates.
Dealers said they were busy, but overall volume was still cautious at 32.8 million shares traded.

Dealers said market heavyweight Telmex, which accounted for 15 percent of all shares traded, was leading the charge, up 10 centavos to 16.90 pesos. The telecomms stock's ADRs were meanwhile up 1/2 to 52-5/8.
Traders said the rally was also buoyed by a recovery in cement maker Cemex and retailers Controladora Comercial Mexicana (Comerci) and holding company Femsa.
Cemex was up 40 centavos to 29.00 pesos and Comerci had gained 10 centavos to 6.26 pesos.
"These stocks were hit very hard and had lagged behind the market," a desk trader said.
